Source: http://www.marijuananews.com

Posted March 17, 2000
A Report from the Florida Journey for Justice.
From Jodi James cfcflo@bellsouth.net for Journey for Justice
See
A Remarkable Record of Activism In Florida
and
Kay Lee Continues Her Journey For Justice At Florida Prison
– What One Person Can Do

(MarijuanaNews note: It is very appropriate that this came to me on the morning of the anniversary of the IOM report. Although the struggle by these brave people is largely ignored by the mainstream media, which are complicit in the crimes of marijuana prohibition, the Internet helps us break out of this isolation.)

J4J Update - Do you watch the movies?

Greetings,

The journey for justice continues. We are only a few days away now, from the start of what is likely to be the most moving thing the participants have ever done. As an organizer, it is one of the most challenging things I could have imagined. We are not inclusive, we have
invited everyone within ear shot to join us in Tallahassee on March 30 as we march to the capitol lawn and hold vigil while patients meet with legislature.

The last two weeks have been a rough, really rough. I have always believed that when you try to do something REALLY good, that all the forces will come against you. We are doing something REALLY REALLY GOOD. Do you remember the movie about Gandhi? The scene near the end were the peaceful people of India walk towards the British soldiers, the British bash them until they can't stand any more, then the women and old men drag the wounded back and a new peaceful man moves forward to be beaten and removed. This war, however, we are sending the wounded in first, to be further beaten and then it is the sick who are dragging them out.
See
Have The Sick And Dying Liberated Alberta Yet?
No, But They Are Working On It.

For six weeks we have asked people to come forward to help with this journey. To offer whatever help they can give. The sick and dying are coming forward, they are willing to be further beaten for the sake of freedom (your and theirs), yet the strong have ignored the needs of the sick.

Six days out and I will mortgage my house to provide rooms for the wheelchair ridden people who are brave enough to come forward. I have spent my savings to buy plane tickets and make fliers. People who are on fixed incomes are making fliers and spending their dimes to get here.

Granted, the work we do is controversial, and everyone might not agree with our methods. I have been challenging people face to face with what are YOU doing to change the laws?

Are you aware that it is the sick, dying and wounded who are protecting your happy home and good job? Here in Melbourne, we have had our phones tapped, our mail interfered with and people sent in to damage our credibility and try to entrap us into committing " crimes ".

Our co-hort (The word of ODC James McDonough's lawyer, Wollerman), Scott Bledsoe has been unlawfully arrested twice.
See
Two Medical Marijuana Trials In Florida: State Drug Czar Says,
" I believe it is yet to be proven there’s anything medical about marijuana. " -- 2 Articles

I understand that some of you can not stand with us physically, your pain or fear prevents it. In Florida, I understand those fears. I have two small children and a not always nice ex-husband, I have dealt with having HRS drug test me ( and my new born child) I have had friends arrested and I have been in prison myself.

What I don't understand is why more people haven't come forward to help, surely you would feel safer standing for yourself then having us stand for you. Why gas vouchers, gift certificates and phone cards haven't been sent yet is a mystery, it is such an anonymous way to help.

We are not funded by the organizations that you are a members of, we are funded by you and by me I guess. We don't have members, by reading this letter we assume you are on your own journey for justice. We commend you for that.

If you are burdened to do more, then please, put the phone card in the mail today, pick up the 10.00 gift certificate at Walmart or Publixs and send it today. Better yet, meet us along the route and journey with us for a day or an hour. Commit yourself to change, tell yourself that you can make a difference and then do.

Follow the journey, many people are giving their all to tell your story.

Jodi James
Melbourne, FL
